title: AliExpress Customs & Duty in Pakistan: What You Actually Pay
summary: What you actually pay on an AliExpress order to Pakistan: duty, taxes, courier clearance fees, and how to estimate the landed cost first.
body_markdown:
The price on an AliExpress listing is not what the order costs you. What you actually pay is four things: the item price, the international shipping charge, whatever customs duty and taxes Pakistan Customs assesses on the parcel, and the courier's clearance and handling fee for doing that paperwork.


There is no single percentage that answers "how much is duty on AliExpress in Pakistan". The rate depends on what the item is classified as, the value it is assessed at, and the tariff in force at the time — and that tariff changes with each finance bill. Anyone quoting you one flat number is quoting a number that was true on some date, for some category, for someone else's parcel.


What you can do is understand how the charge is built, know which categories get hit hardest, and check the current rate before you order rather than at your door.


## The four things that add up to your landed cost


Work out all four before you decide the order is cheap. Resellers call the total the landed cost, and it is the only number that matters.


- **Item price.** What the listing shows, converted to PKR at whatever rate your card issuer uses on the day — not the rate you looked up that morning.
- **International shipping.** Sometimes shown as free and priced into the item, sometimes charged separately, and usually much higher for express than for standard economy shipping.
- **Customs duty and taxes.** Assessed on arrival in Pakistan, against the value and classification customs applies to your parcel. This is the part nobody can quote in advance with certainty.
- **Courier clearance and handling.** The courier acts as your clearing agent, files the paperwork, pays the duty on your behalf and then collects it from you — plus its own fee — before it releases the parcel.


The last two are why an order that looked cheap at checkout can arrive with a bill attached. They are also why two people who ordered the same product can pay different totals.


## How an incoming parcel is actually assessed


The mechanics are the same whether the parcel came from AliExpress or anywhere else abroad.


### Declared value versus assessed value


The seller writes a declared value on the customs declaration. Customs is not obliged to accept it. If the declared figure looks unrealistic for the goods, the parcel is assessed at a value customs considers reasonable, and duty is calculated on that instead. This is the single biggest reason a "the seller marked it as a $2 gift" plan does not work the way people expect.


### Classification


Every imported item falls under a tariff classification, and the classification — not your description of it — sets the rate. A phone accessory, a cosmetic, a garment and a battery-powered device are four different categories with four different treatments. This is why one person's experience with a phone case tells you nothing useful about your order of hair styling tools.


### Who collects it


You almost never deal with Pakistan Customs directly on a courier parcel. The courier clears it, pays, and then presents you the total at delivery or asks for payment before it schedules delivery. Keep whatever receipt or breakdown it gives you; it is the only record of what you were charged and why.


### Low-value parcels


Pakistan has treated small personal parcels differently from commercial consignments, and the threshold and the rules around it have been revised more than once. Do not rely on a figure someone posted in a forum two years ago. If the difference between paying duty and not paying it decides your order, check the current position before you buy — the tariff and the courier's own rate sheet are the two places that are actually current.


## Where to check the real number before you order


Three sources, in order of usefulness:


- **The current Pakistan Customs tariff.** The published tariff is the authority for what a category attracts. It is dry, but it is the only source that is not someone's anecdote.
- **The courier handling the shipment.** Express couriers will tell you their clearance and handling charge, and can usually indicate how a category is normally treated. Ask before the parcel is in the air, not after.
- **Someone who has imported the same category recently.** Useful as a sanity check on the order of magnitude. Useless as a precise figure, because their declared value and route were not yours.


One habit worth building: write down the item price, the shipping, and your estimate of duty and handling *before* you order, then write down what you actually paid when it arrives. After three or four orders in a category you will have a realistic multiplier for that category, which is worth more than any published rule of thumb.


## Why the same product costs two people different amounts


- **Shipping method.** Economy postal routes and express courier routes are cleared differently and carry different handling charges.
- **Declared value.** Different sellers declare differently, and customs may reassess either way.
- **Where it actually shipped from.** Some AliExpress listings ship from a warehouse inside or near your region rather than from China. That parcel takes a different route and a different charge.
- **Whether it arrived alone or with other parcels.** Several items consolidated into one consignment are assessed as one consignment.
- **Timing.** Rates and thresholds change with policy. An order that cleared cheaply last year is not a forecast for this year.


## The categories that cause the most trouble


Some things are more expensive to import than the sticker suggests, and some are more trouble than they are worth.


- **Mobile phones.** A phone brought into Pakistan has to be registered with PTA before it will work on local networks, and that registration cost is separate from customs duty and varies by device. A phone that seems cheap on AliExpress is frequently not cheap once it is legal to use.
- **Electronics and battery-powered devices.** Lithium batteries carry shipping restrictions on top of duty, so the route is slower and the options are fewer.
- **Branded goods.** Anything that looks like a counterfeit of a protected brand is a problem at the border, not a bargain.
- **Cosmetics, supplements and anything ingestible or applied to skin.** These sit under regulatory regimes beyond ordinary duty, and personal imports are frequently held.
- **Liquids, aerosols and flammables.** Often refused at the shipping stage before customs is even a question.
- **Low-value accessories.** The cheapest category to import and the one where AliExpress genuinely competes — a small, light, non-branded, non-battery item is the easy case.


## Why under-declaring backfires


The advice to ask a seller to mark a parcel as a low-value gift circulates constantly. It is a bad trade for three reasons.


First, customs can reassess the value anyway, so the saving may not happen. Second, if the parcel is held for misdeclaration, you lose weeks and may pay a penalty on top of the duty you were avoiding. Third, your insurance and any dispute claim are pegged to the declared value — a parcel declared at a token amount and then lost is compensated at a token amount.


For a one-off personal order, the downside is a delay and a bad afternoon. If you are buying stock to sell, a held consignment is money frozen for an unknown number of weeks, which is the risk that actually kills small resellers.


## Estimating before you order: a short checklist


- Convert the item price at today's rate, not last month's.
- Add the shipping charge shown at checkout — and check whether "free shipping" is the slow route.
- Identify the category honestly. Is it an accessory, an electronic device, a cosmetic, a branded item?
- Check the current tariff treatment for that category and the courier's clearance fee.
- Add a buffer. If your estimate makes the order only slightly cheaper than buying it locally, it is not cheaper.
- Decide whether you can wait. Cross-border delivery is measured in weeks, and a held parcel adds more.


If the total lands close to the local price, buy locally. Speed, a return path and a bill you can predict are all worth something.

## If you are importing to resell


The calculation changes when the parcel is stock rather than a purchase. Three things matter more than the duty rate itself.


**Predictability beats the lowest number.** You cannot price a product for a customer if you do not know your landed cost within a reasonable range. A slightly higher cost you can quote today is more useful than a lower one you discover at the door.


**Cash tied up in a held consignment is the real cost.** A parcel stuck in clearance is capital you cannot use, in a business that runs on turning stock over.


**Minimum order quantities multiply the risk.** Importing yourself usually means buying in quantity to make the freight worthwhile — which means committing money to a product before you know it sells. ## Frequently asked questions


### How much is customs duty on AliExpress orders in Pakistan?


There is no single rate. Duty and taxes depend on how the item is classified, the value customs assesses it at, and the tariff in force when it arrives. Check the current Pakistan Customs tariff for your category and ask the courier for its clearance and handling charge before ordering.


### Do all AliExpress parcels get charged customs in Pakistan?


No, and that is exactly why the question is confusing. Small low-value parcels sometimes arrive with nothing to pay, while a similar-looking parcel is assessed. Route, declared value, category and current policy all feed into it, so treat a duty-free delivery as luck rather than as the rule.


### Can I ask the seller to declare a lower value to avoid duty?


You can, and it is a poor trade. Customs can reassess the value regardless, a misdeclared parcel can be held or penalised, and your compensation if the parcel is lost is limited to the declared amount.


### Who collects the duty — customs or the courier?


In practice the courier. It clears the parcel, pays the assessed duty and taxes, and collects that plus its own handling fee from you before delivering. Ask for the breakdown and keep it.


### Is it cheaper to buy from AliExpress or locally in Pakistan?


Compare landed costs, not stickers. Small, light, non-branded accessories are often genuinely cheaper imported. Once duty, handling, shipping and the wait are added, many mid-priced items are not — and a local order that arrives in 3–5 days with a return path attached is frequently the better buy.


### How do I avoid customs surprises entirely?


Buy through a route where the import is already handled and the price you see is the price you pay. Markaz China quotes in PKR, handles shipping and clearance, delivers in about 10–17 days and takes cash on delivery, so there is no separate bill from a courier at your door.
